statement: On one side of a street the houses are numbered 1, 3, 5, 7 and so on. What is the number of the 8th house?

choices.misconception: I gave 8 itself, which is the house's place in the row, not its number.
I counted one house too few and found the number of the 7th house.
I doubled 8, but that gives an even number, and this side has only odd numbers.
I counted one house too many and found the number of the 9th house.

hints: Count the odd numbers on your fingers.
The house numbers are the odd numbers in order. Count along them one house at a time, keeping track of which house you are on, until you reach the 8th.
The first seven houses are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. The next odd number is the 8th house.

solutions.reliable: List the odd numbers and count houses: 1 (1st), 3 (2nd), 5 (3rd), 7 (4th), 9 (5th), 11 (6th), 13 (7th), 15 (8th). The 8th house is number 15. The idea to keep: the odd numbers go up in 2s, and keeping count of the places stops you landing one too far or one too short.
solutions.elegant: The 8th even number is 16, and each odd number is one less than the even number in the same place, so the 8th odd number is 15.

whyOnTest: Odd numbers in order are a short counting chain, and keeping place and value apart is what the question checks.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
